name: Body Integrity Dysphoria

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Body Integrity Dysphoria

criteria.description: Persistent and intense desire to amputate or disable a healthy limb or body part
Clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning due to the desire
Absence of psychotic disorders or other neurological conditions explaining the desire
Onset of symptoms typically in early adulthood or adolescence
Experience of incongruence between physical body and internal body image

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: persistent desire for amputation/disability, significant distress or impairment, and exclusion of psychotic or neurological disorders
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnostic criteria are evolving; differential diagnosis with somatoparaphrenia and other identity disorders is essential.

searchTerms: muscle weakness in arms or legs

imaging: Functional MRI may show altered parietal lobe activity related to body representation
other: Clinical diagnosis based on history and symptomatology

distinguishingFeatures: Typically occurs after right hemisphere brain injury
Denial of ownership of a limb without desire for amputation
Preoccupation with perceived physical defects not related to limb integrity
Absence of desire for amputation or disability
Focus on appearance rather than body integrity

redFlags: Self-inflicted injury or attempts at amputation
Severe functional impairment or suicidal ideation
references: First MC, Fisher AD. Body Integrity Dysphoria: Clinical and Ethical Issues. Curr Psychiatry Rep. 2019;21(9):87.
Brugger P, Lenggenhager B, Giummarra MJ. Body Integrity Dysphoria: A Neurological and Psychological Disorder. Lancet Psychiatry. 2017;4(10):903-912.
American Psychiatric Association. Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition (DSM-5). 2013.
